title: Sunrise Ops - Immersion Onboarding Kickoff
summary: Introductory onboarding kickoff for Sunrise Ops. Covered success metrics, technical intake (VPC, SSO, data retention), staging plan and pilot runbook. Discussed latency SLAs, dedicated vs hosted options, KMS integration and compliance evidence. Agreed next steps: share access matrix, Redwood security pack, schedule a dedicated SE deep-dive and set pilot window for July 6-17.
transcript:
Header:
- Date: 2026-06-26
- Start: 15:00 UTC
- Duration: ~52 minutes
- Recorders: Fireflies / Redwood Console Integration
- Attendees: Maya C, Rafael O, Priya N, Jon P; Ellen P, Marcus L, Danielle R, Tariq A, Olivia G

Auto-summary (may be rough): Kickoff, align success metrics, list out security docs and pilot runbook, network intake and access matrix.

00:00 Speaker 1 (Maya Chen): hey everyone thanks for joining on time, appreciate it. quick round of intros then we'll get into goals for the onboarding and the pilot dates.
00:19 Speaker 2 (Ellen Park): hi im ellen, cto at sunrise ops, looking forward to getting this in staging; i want to make sure latency is solid, we have call center use cases.
00:35 Speaker 3 (Rafael Ortiz): awesome, thanks ellen. im rafael, customer success, i'll be your day-to-day. we'll own the runbook with you.
00:48 Speaker 4 (Marcus Lee): marcus, platform eng, i'll lead infra. we run k8s on aws but we also have a strict vpc peer policy.
01:05 Speaker 5 (Priya Nair): priya here, solutions eng. i'll handle the technical onboarding and bench tests. quick note: our staging plan usually requires ip allowlist and cert rotation.
01:26 Speaker 6 (Danielle Ruiz): danielle, security. curious about KMS integration and audit logs — SOC2 evidence, please.
01:40 Speaker 1 (Maya): great, i'll share the security pack and SOC2 artifacts today after the call, and our se priya will book a deep-dive for network details.
01:51 Speaker 7 (Olivia Grant): olivia, pm — we want the pilot to run for about 2 weeks and validate p95 latency and end-to-end cost.
02:06 Speaker 8 (Tariq Ahmed): tariq, data eng — we care about data residency; some tokens persist in cache, how long does it live?

03:12 Speaker 3 (Priya): good question — by default cache TTL is short, but we'll propose a KV cache policy for your workflow. details in the runbook. there might be some mis-match of names here, sorry — kv cahse sometimes transcribed weird.
03:38 Speaker 2 (Ellen): cool. what about dedicated vs hosted? our compliance team prefers dedicated, but cost is a concern.
03:54 Speaker 4 (Marcus): yeah and we have burst periods, so autoscale matters.
04:10 Speaker 1 (Maya): high level — hosted is fastest to start, dedicated gives you isolation and predictable throughput. we can show a cost projection. we recommend a short hosted pilot to validate prompts then shift to dedicated if throughput and isolation needs justify it.
04:35 Speaker 5 (Priya): for call center latency, we should test 512 token context and end-to-end p95 under concurrent sessions. i'll run a benchmark plan with you.
05:02 Speaker 6 (Danielle): encryption at rest, does redwood integrate with our KMS? we require CMK in our account.
05:17 Speaker 3 (Priya): yes, we support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM for private deployments; for hosted we offer envelope encryption and can discuss bring-your-own-key options.
05:34 Speaker 1 (Maya): i'll attach our KMS matrix in the docs.

06:05 Speaker 4 (Marcus): network wise, we want traffic to stay inside our vpc; do you support VPC peering or privatelink?
06:20 Speaker 3 (Priya): both are supported depending on the deployment. private (VPC) deploy uses VPC peering or AWS PrivateLink, sometimes transit gateway for multi-account. note: some words in the transcript may be off, like pry-a vs priya, sorry for the auto caption typos.
06:47 Speaker 8 (Tariq): data residency — we need EU data to stay within eu-west-1 for certain flows. can we pin region?
06:58 Speaker 1 (Maya): yes, we can pin region for the pilot; dedicated capacity and private deployments support region pinning. hosted api also can be routed to region tiers.

08:05 Speaker 5 (Priya): going into the pilot plan: propose timeline July 6 start, two week pilot July 6-17. week one: seed data, connect staging, run baseline prompts. week two: load tests and quality evals. we'll measure p95 latency, token cost per session, and quality regressions with your eval set.
08:36 Speaker 7 (Olivia): that timeline works for our product team.
08:45 Speaker 2 (Ellen): prescribe what success looks like — p95 under 300ms for single-turn? is that realistic?
09:02 Speaker 3 (Priya): single-turn 300ms is aggressive for remote hosted with long contexts; for optimized runtime with batching and quantized model we can aim for p95 400-600ms depending on model and sequence length. we should pick model variant and target.
09:22 Speaker 4 (Marcus): list the tradeoffs — lower latency often means smaller batch sizes, higher cost.
09:33 Speaker 1 (Maya): exactly — tradeoff is cost vs latency vs throughput. redwood optimize will give suggestions; we'll include a config proposal.

10:05 Speaker 6 (Danielle): audit logs and user access — can we export audit logs to our SIEM?
10:16 Speaker 3 (Priya): yes, audit logs can be exported via SIEM connector or delivered to your S3 with cross-account role. retention policies are configurable for private, dedicated, hosted has standard retention windows.
10:32 Speaker 6 (Danielle): also need SSO — SAML with SCIM provisioning ideally.
10:40 Speaker 1 (Maya): we support SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning. jon (docs) will share the SCIM endpoints and sample manifests.

12:05 Speaker 9 (Jon Park): i'll drop a step-by-step doc and the access matrix template; expect it in slack and email.
12:20 Speaker 2 (Ellen): regarding data retention we have a 90 day rule for transcripts, anything beyond needs legal approval. can we set TTLs?
12:34 Speaker 3 (Priya): you can configure retention at route level; for the pilot we can set a 30-day rolling window and iterate. note that cache eviction and KV policies may differ.

14:00 Speaker 5 (Priya): ok technical intake checklist: 1) VPC connection method (peering/privatelink/transit), 2) SAML metadata, 3) KMS key ARN or envelope config, 4) list of IP ranges for allowlist, 5) pilot eval prompts and dataset (redacted).
14:28 Speaker 8 (Tariq): about evals — we will share a curated set of 150 prompts, some PII redacted. quality monitoring alerts should trigger on regression.
14:45 Speaker 1 (Maya): we'll wire up quality monitors and create a baseline run. redwood optimize can surface quantization suggestions to reduce cost.

16:10 Speaker 4 (Marcus): SLA question — for dedicated, what's the uptime and latency SLO?
16:21 Speaker 3 (Priya): dedicated has an SLA of 99.9% uptime and latency targets per model profile; we'll include the exact SLA in the contract.
16:36 Speaker 6 (Danielle): legal wants to see subprocessor list and data flow diagrams.
16:46 Speaker 1 (Maya): i'll share the subprocessors doc and PCI/ISO cert links.

18:00 Speaker 7 (Olivia): who will own the pilot runbook on your side?
18:08 Speaker 2 (Rafael): i'll coordinate and be primary contact; priya will lead technical tasks.
18:16 Speaker 2 (Ellen): on our side olivia and marcus will be leads, danielle on security oversight.

20:00 Speaker 3 (Priya): ok let's talk rough bench numbers — if you test 100 concurrent call center sessions with 256 tokens, we should expect throughput of X under dedicated capac. (auto-transcribe shows X as placeholder) we'll schedule a load test and capture p50/p95/p99.
20:30 Speaker 4 (Marcus): can you send an example benchmark spreadsheet?
20:38 Speaker 9 (Jon): yes, will share benchmark template and sample results from a similar customer.

22:12 Speaker 5 (Priya): also note model selection: we can start with a mid-size open model to control cost then swap to a higher-accuracy variant if needed. model rollouts support canary and A/B.
22:41 Speaker 1 (Maya): good to highlight — safe rollouts are built in so you can test in prod with fallback policies.

24:00 Speaker 6 (Danielle): still worried about keys — onboarding for KMS may take lead time, who sets it up?
24:12 Speaker 3 (Priya): typically the customer's security creates the CMK and grants Redwood a key policy cross-account role; we'll provide terraform snippets to expedite.

26:00 Speaker 7 (Olivia): training for our ops team — do you offer runbook walk-through and playbook training?
26:12 Speaker 2 (Rafael): yes, we run a 2-hour enablement and hand-off session during pilot week one.

28:20 Speaker 5 (Priya): anything else on integrations? observability — we'll hook into your datadog or prometheus. which do you use?
28:31 Speaker 4 (Marcus): datadog primarily; we also have an internal pager duty routing.
28:42 Speaker 3 (Priya): great, we have datadog metrics and tracing hooks; we'll send a sample dashboard.

30:00 Speaker 1 (Maya): i want to make sure we capture risks: 1) KMS lead time, 2) VPC connectivity approvals, 3) pilot dataset availability. any more?
30:18 Speaker 2 (Ellen): approvals from compliance could delay by 2 weeks.
30:27 Speaker 1 (Maya): noted.

32:05 Speaker 9 (Jon): sharing tentative doc links: - Security pack (link will be shared) - Benchmark template - Access matrix template - Pilot runbook skeleton
32:30 Speaker 7 (Olivia): please share those to the project channel.

34:10 Speaker 3 (Priya): quick demo note — not doing a live demo today to keep this to intake; we'll do a recorded benchmark and a live se deep-dive next week.
34:29 Speaker 1 (Maya): ok next steps we'll list those in the recap.

36:00 Speaker 6 (Danielle): competitors — we've looked at two vendors: fastserve.ai and cloudendpoints. concern is vendor lock in and SSO integration.
36:18 Speaker 1 (Maya): we can show how Redwood avoids lock-in via model catalog and deployment abstraction.

38:00 Speaker 5 (Priya): timeline recap: Task 1: security docs & SOC2 (Maya) by EOD; Task 2: send access matrix (Jon) by tomorrow; Task 3: SE deep-dive for VPC (Priya) — propose July 1; Task 4: pilot start July 6.
38:30 Speaker 2 (Ellen): July 1 deep-dive works for compliance and infra.
38:40 Speaker 1 (Maya): Rafael will send calendar invites after the call.

40:20 Speaker 4 (Marcus): one more technical: does Redwood support prewarming GPU pools for burst traffic?
40:34 Speaker 3 (Priya): yes, dedicated can be prewarmed and autoscaler has warmup options, also burst capacity for short spikes. we'll include config examples.

42:05 Speaker 7 (Olivia): cost estimate — can you provide a ballpark for two-week pilot and a monthly committed estimate for dedicated?
42:20 Speaker 1 (Maya): yes we'll send pricing ranges; for pilot we usually provide an estimated burn for hosted tests; for committed dedicated we'll share T-shirt sizing and pricing tiers.

44:00 Speaker 6 (Danielle): compliance question: do you have ISO27001?
44:08 Speaker 1 (Maya): yes, plus SOC2 type II. doc pack will include those certs.

46:00 Speaker 9 (Jon): i'll also include a runbook template for incident playbooks and an ops handoff checklist.
46:18 Speaker 2 (Ellen): great.

48:00 Speaker 1 (Maya): ok hands-on next steps we'll list out at the end. any outstanding blockers?
48:10 Speaker 4 (Marcus): only approvals for peering.
48:17 Speaker 6 (Danielle): KMS creation calendar lead time.
48:24 Speaker 2 (Ellen): none other.

50:00 Speaker 1 (Maya): thanks everyone for the time. recap in chat and email. Rafael will coordinate pilot kickoff and invites.
50:15 Speaker 2 (Rafael): thanks all, look forward to the deep-dive.
50:22 Speaker 7 (Olivia): thanks.
50:30 Speaker 2 (Ellen): bye.

Auto transcription notes: occasional mis-heard words (e.g., "kv cahse" instead of "KV cache"). Some speaker labels simplified by the recorder.
